Implementation report

Board item management: editing, actions and conversation controls

Issue #6570 asked for item editing, issue and discussion management, and pull-request actions across the source board. This is what was built, how each provider behaves, and what was verified on real hosts.

Click any screenshot to open it full size: the arrow keys step through the captures and Esc closes it.

Scope

Everything on this page lives behind the existing board surfaces: the desktop and phone board, the Tracker repository tab, and the branch's pull-request tab. The reference picker stays read-only, and a linked item never offers a write. Every write goes through the shared mutation executor: an idempotency key and digest are claimed before the provider call, a repeated key replays instead of writing twice, and an interrupted write reconciles to a sticky outcome-unknown rather than a guess.

Provider matrix

Built-in providers implement the same operations through their own APIs or the shared standard mutation table; extension providers declare capabilities and receive the standard routes. Gerrit answers 501 by capability, which is a deliberate, visible unsupported state rather than a missing button.

Board, filter menu and remembered filters

Labels narrow the list on the host, not in the browser: GitHub through label:"…" search qualifiers (AND), GitLab through a comma-joined labels= (AND), Gitea through label names on /issues (AND). Because pulls.list has no label parameter at all, a label-narrowed pull list deliberately switches to GitHub's search endpoint instead of filtering one returned page and showing sparse results. An unfiltered read sends exactly the payload it did before this work.

There is one filter control, not three: status, people and the repository's labels live in the same panel, and the labels section reads the host's catalogue when the panel opens — a search field, a check per label, a Clear row, a spinner while loading, and a kept selection when the read fails or the host stops listing a label. The trigger names what is applied in its summary (Open · bug, then Open · bug +2) and lists them all in its tooltip; no second button sits beside it.

The selection is remembered per resolved repository and tab, in openchamber.repositoryFilters.v1, keyed by provider, instance and owner/repo: a fork clone and its upstream share one entry, two clones of one remote share one, and another repository never inherits the labels picked in this one. It is restored when that repository's panel opens; labels are capped at 20 and the store at 500 entries, a malformed entry is dropped without touching the rest, and the list across repositories has no entry at all. GitHub additionally parses qualifiers out of the search text, so where a typed is:closed or assignee: decides a field the matching control reads Status · from search and is disabled rather than staying clickable and inert; the field names the qualifiers in its placeholder, and only on a host that actually parses them.

Editing an item's text

A pencil beside refresh turns the title into a one-line field and the description into a Markdown editor. Save and Cancel sit in the title row where the edit starts; Enter saves from the single-line title, Enter breaks the line in the description, and Mod+Enter saves from either. The description is Markdown source, so it uses the composer's CodeMirror with an empty resolution context: @name is the host's user, not an agent, and a file path is not a workspace file. Pasted images are not taken, because a source-control write has nowhere to put an upload. The editor is offered only when the detail says this account may update the item, the provider advertises the capability, the item is not linked, and the list body is not a truncated body without a full detail body — saving a 20 000-character cut would silently overwrite the rest of the text.

Real host: typing into the description and pressing Ctrl+Enter updated issue body on GitHub; pressing Enter in the title saved a new title, later restored.

Conversation comments

A comment's menu appears on hover beside the attach action: Edit opens the text in the same Markdown editor, Delete asks first in the app's dialog. Both are offered only on a conversation comment the host gave an id to — never on a review-thread comment or a verdict — and only where the surface passes write actions and the item is not linked. The comment's body is edited in the composer editor too (Enter breaks the line, Mod+Enter saves), while the reply box keeps its existing textarea.

Assignees, labels and lock

Assignees are a metadata row with the same searchable picker as labels: the candidates come from the project's reviewer endpoint, and the write replaces the whole set. The pencil appears only when that read answers with someone to pick; a host that refuses it keeps the row read-only from the detail. Labels are committed as one set when the popup closes. Lock and unlock sit with refresh, send the opposite of what the detail reported, and never flip before the host's read comes back.

Cross-references on the timeline

When another issue or pull request mentions this item, that mention appears in the conversation timeline in the order it happened, between comments and commits: the actor, when it happened, and a chip naming the item. A chip shows #N in the item's own repository and owner/repo#N for another one, carries the title as a tooltip where the host sends one, and opens from the chat like the item's other links. GitHub reads the newest 20 CrossReferencedEvent timeline items on issues and pull requests; GitLab parses the mentioned in issue #N / merge request !N system notes (cross-project and several in one note included, commits ignored); Gitea reads issue_ref / pull_ref entries from the issue timeline. GitHub exposes no timeline for Discussions, so a discussion shows none rather than a guessed list.

State and close reason

Where the host advertises an issue close reason, the state menu offers two closes: completed and not planned. GitHub carries it as state_reason, honoured only when the same call changes state — a reopen carrying a reason is refused, and a pull request is refused entirely because pulls.update has no such field. Restart reconciliation compares the read-back reason, so an interrupted close is never recorded as a different outcome.

Pull request actions

The base branch carries a pencil after the branch it points at, reading the repository's branches on open and leaving out the current base. One pick is one write; afterwards the detail and the list row are both re-read, because the row's own base is the target of every later write. Update branch merges the base into head on GitHub and Gitea; GitLab only offers a rebase, so the two entries exist separately and neither toast claims the branch is already in sync.

The first Update branch was refused with HTTP 422 and the host's own message, merge conflict between base and head: a real conflict, surfaced unchanged and never recorded as success. After resolving it, the same action succeeded.

Discussions

GitHub-only. Upvote reads viewerHasUpvoted from the detail and writes add/remove by node id; the count only changes after the host's read. Category change lists the host's categories, excludes the current one, and reconciles by comparing the read-back category id. Lock and subscription reuse the conversation controls, so a discussion gains them with no separate implementation.

Static checks and unit tests are necessary, not sufficient; the writes below were driven through a real dev server and a real GitHub account, and the resulting state was read back with the GitHub API.

Known limits and decisions

Subscription needs a token scope

GitHub's subscription write requires the notifications scope. A token with only repo gets a 422 on click; the control stays visible because a credential does not carry its scopes, so the honest fallback is the host's own message with the item left unchanged.

A transient read is retried once

During real use a details read failed with ECONNRESET — a pooled connection closed under it — and the preview correctly showed a failure. A bound GET changed nothing, so the shell now reads once more on ECONNRESET, EPIPE, ECONNREFUSED or a timeout before answering a failure.

Deliberately not built

Reactions, milestone / due date / projects, team reviewers, explicit auto-merge, re-run checks and adding linked issues. Merge-when-ready already enables auto-merge when a merge is blocked, so a second control would be a duplicate.
